newsitem.title: USA: Florida court sets January hearing in Bucs lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Florida court sets January hearing in Bucs lawsuit.

text.p: An appeals court scheduled a Jan 14 hearing in a lawsuit seeking to block bond financing of a new stadium for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers football team, a court clerk said Thursday.
The move by the 2nd District Court of Appeal in Lakeland could force stadium construction to halt because the current construction fund will be depleted by then.

Hillsborough County attorneys have advised the county not to sell bonds for the $168 million stadium until the litigation is resolved. They sought unsuccessfully to waive oral arguments in order to speed up the ruling.

The county had hoped to sell revenue bonds for the project by the end of the year, fearing the sale would be blocked if Congress adopts U.S. Sen. Patrick Moynihan's, D-N.Y., bill to block public funding of professional sports facilities in January.
Voters adopted a Sept 3 referendum raising the county's sales tax by a half-cent to fund schools, public safety projects and the stadium.

Former Tampa Mayor William Poe sued to block the stadium project, claiming it would unconstitutionally use public money to benefit the for-profit football team. He appealed after a lower court dismissed the lawsuit.
If the stadium is not finished in time for the 1998 football season, the county would have to pay the team $437,500 for each game that must be played elsewhere.
